title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Several Overpayments Owed by One Claimant
content:
**1.** A claimant may owe several Benefit Overpayment Accounts at once, on the same claim or on different claims. The number of overpayments one claimant may owe is not capped.

**2.** An overpayment is established only once for the same claim, cause and first overpaid week.

**3.** A second issue affecting the same weeks is established as its own overpayment only for amounts not already established. An overpayment that was cancelled does not block a new determination on a different cause.

**4.** How recoveries are shared among several open overpayments is decided by the Department's recovery order for open overpayments.

## Applying clause 2

The test in clause 2 is made on the Department's own overpayment records before an overpayment is established, never on the claimant's account of events. The three items compared are the claim, the cause and the first overpaid week of the proposed overpayment against the same three items on the claimant's existing overpayment records. An existing record counts for the comparison when its status is established, in recovery, waiver pending, suspended, paid in full, waived or written off.

| Existing record on the same claim | Same cause | Same first overpaid week | A further overpayment for the same issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes, in one of the statuses listed above | Yes | Yes | Not established |
| Yes | No | Yes | Clause 2 does not bar it |
| Yes | Yes | No | Clause 2 does not bar it |

## Cases

*Hypothetical:* a claimant already owes an overpayment on claim A for earnings misreported, beginning with the week ending 7 March. A second overpayment on claim A for earnings misreported beginning with the week ending 7 March is not established; the issue is already established.

*Hypothetical:* the same claimant is later found ineligible on claim A for a separation issue covering some of the same weeks. The separation issue is a second issue; it is established as its own overpayment only for amounts not already established under the first.
